$comment: GET /{leadId}, read from Meta's Retrieving Leads guide. The webhook carries ids and nothing else, so this is the half that produces data a flow can act on -- and it is a separate node rather than being folded into the trigger, for the same reason Instagram's publish is two actions: it is what the API is, and a lead can also be fetched by id without any webhook having fired.
title: Facebook lead
description: Read one lead's answers by id. Pair this with the `leadgen` trigger, whose delivery carries only the id.

request.$pathComment: A lead is addressed at the ROOT of the Graph API by its own id -- there is no /{formId}/leads/{leadId} route. Meta's ids are globally unique across object types, which is why /{id} works at all and why passing the wrong kind of id returns a different object rather than a 404.

config.label: Lead ID
config.description: From the `leadgen_id` on a `leadgen` delivery. It is not the form id and not the ad id -- both are also numeric, and passing one of those returns THAT object rather than an error.

outputShape.description: ISO 8601 with an offset, e.g. 2026-08-24T09:15:00+0000. NOT the unix seconds the webhook sends for the same event.
The ad that produced the lead. Absent for an organic submission.

The answers, as a LIST of { name, values } rather than a map — so `field_data.email` does not exist and reading one means finding the entry whose `name` matches. The names are the form's own field keys, which the advertiser chose, so they differ between forms on the same Page. `values` is an array even for a single-answer question.
